Incorporating the Beige Book, the FOMC’s assessment of strong economic activity and a tight labor market is corroborated by broad-based growth reported across multiple Districts (including Boston, Philadelphia, Cleveland, St. Louis, Kansas City, Dallas, Atlanta, Chicago, and San Francisco). Labor markets remain tight with ongoing job gains, and firms are using nonwage compensation—bonuses, profit-sharing, health benefits, and paid vacation—to attract/retain workers, consistent with continued labor-market strength. Price pressures are mixed across Districts; falling fuel prices offset some broader cost increases even as house prices continue to rise, aligning with inflation running near 2 percent and stable longer-term expectations.

However, bank lending conditions from SLOOS point to tighter credit supply—particularly for C&I and construction/land development loans—and softer loan demand, which likely weighs on business investment and commercial real estate. That tightening, alongside late-2018 market volatility, reinforces the statement’s observation that business fixed investment has moderated and argues for a more cautious policy stance than “some further gradual increases” alone would suggest.

Net tone: still positive on growth and labor, with inflation anchored, but notably more cautious given tighter bank lending standards and softer loan demand. Adjusting sentiment modestly lower.
